76749.subject: Robinhood’s Q2 2026: a 44% EPS beat, a $106M gain that’s already gone & why HOOD stock fell anyway 🏹📉; Revolut o…
76749.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1107

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Friday! Today, we're diving deep into Robinhood's latest financials to see why a monster quarter still couldn't stop the stock from falling (breaking down the most important facts & figures from Robinhood's Q2 2026, including the $106M gain that vanished before the earnings call even started, to see whether $HOOD  is still worth your time & money + bonus guide on how to Turn Claude Opus 5 Into a Financial Analyst That Never Sleeps [ https://substack.com/redirect/ccd7d9bd-dd57-4341-9a2a-19ef3122d122?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and fintech giant Revolut, which just opened private market access to 75 million users (the mechanics, why the timing is awkward, the OpenAI deal that dropped 3 days later & what it all means for Revolut's $150-200B IPO play + bonus deep dives into Revolut [ https://substack.com/redirect/81ca806b-2569-4836-94d6-b64ede458ee8?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] & the AI Monopoly Playbook [ https://substack.com/redirect/068e1e8f-ac53-4a9b-9c9f-8b6689e3d072?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s just jump straight into the intriguing stuff 🌶️
Robinhood’s Q2 2026: a 44% EPS beat, a $106M gain that’s already gone & why HOOD stock fell anyway 🏹📉
Earnings time 🤑 Stock trading giant Robinhood $HOOD  just delivered the blowout quarter everyone wanted, and the stock fell anyway.
Revenues rose 32% year-over-year to a record $1.31B, and diluted EPS of $0.62 crushed the $0.41-0.43 consensus by 44-51%. Net deposits hit a record $21.7B, platform assets a record $369B, Gold subscribers a record 4.8M, and management lowered the full-year expense guide while calling the business “firing on all cylinders.” Not too shabby!
And still the stock dropped 3.15% on the day and another 2.69% the next morning to $87.42 - 24% below its July 15 close & 43% below its 52-week high 🤷‍♂️
But the most important number of the quarter wasn’t the beat, and it wasn’t the selloff either. It was $4 billion - the pace of new customer deposits in July, disclosed on the earnings call. Some context here: net deposits are the metric management itself calls the engine of the business, because deposits become platform assets, and assets become trading, margin lending and Gold subscriptions. Robinhood targets roughly 20% annual growth on this line, and Q2 delivered 28%. Except that $10.1B of the quarter’s $21.7B arrived in June alone, and July’s ~$4B pace works out to just 13% annualised - the slowest month of the year, and slower than every single quarter of the past two years. Put simply, the record quarter ended the moment the quarter did.

## ChatGPT made itself cheaper

Your subscription price didn't move. What changed is that Luna and Terra now eat fewer credits inside Codex and ChatGPT Work, so the same plan stretches further.

Here's who found the savings. Inside a human-led process, GPT-5.6 Sol rewrote and optimized OpenAI's production kernels, then designed and ran hundreds of experiments on token generation.

That work cut the cost of serving the model by 20% and improved token-generation efficiency by more than 15%. OpenAI turned it into a price cut the next day.

Luna is the one to watch. On professional work it beats Fable 5 at an estimated cost per task nearly 99% lower, and runs year-ago frontier performance at roughly 6 cents on the dollar.

Replit's president called it the closest anyone has come to intelligence too cheap to meter.

Sol got Fast mode instead, 2.5 times quicker at double the price.

Five things happened this week. Each one changes how AI- and blockchain-driven companies operate, spend, and manage risk. Here is what every operator, founder, and investor needs to know. ◆ DEVELOPMENT 01 - Alphabet just had its worst trading day in over a year, and it was self-inflicted . Alphabet shares fell more than 7% after the company raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to as much as $205 billion and reported negative free cash flow for the first time since its 2004 IPO. Meta dropped nearly 10% the same week on the same worry: AI infrastructure spending is now eating into cash generation faster than the market wants to tolerate. Together, Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta are projected to spend roughly $724 billion on capex this year, and analysts expect that to approach $950 billion in 2027. Why it matters: the unwritten deal between investors and Big Tech spend whatever you want on AI as long as revenue keeps climbing just broke. The Ment Tech perspective: we help clients model AI infrastructure spend against actual revenue timelines before committing, so the build-vs-buy decision holds up under exactly this kind of investor scrutiny. ◆ DEVELOPMENT 02 - Apple did nothing, and it's now worth more than almost anyone else on Earth While its Magnificent Seven peers got punished for AI capex, Apple's stock climbed 15% in July alone and its market cap crossed $5 trillion, putting it alongside Nvidia as one of only two companies to hit that mark. Apple's strategy has been to avoid heavy in-house AI infrastructure spending and instead partner with outside model developers to power its services. Why it matters: the market just rewarded restraint over ambition, for the first time in this entire AI cycle. The Ment Tech perspective: not every client needs to own the infrastructure to win with AI. We build partnership-first architectures for clients who want AI capability without the balance-sheet risk that comes with owning the compute. ◆ DEVELOPMENT 03- Chip stocks just had their worst month since 2022 The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) is down 17% in July after being up 101% in the first half of the year, on pace for its worst month since June 2022.
